ink.note: Body text, primary button ground, and focus ring. The system's only 'brand' colour, and deliberately a neutral so no insurer tenant owns it. Ink and paper swap roles in dark mode rather than dimming.

ink-inverse.note: Text on a Ledger Ink ground. Never used as a surface.

paper.note: Every panel, table, card and slide-over surface. In dark mode it sits one step ABOVE the page ground, so a panel reads as laid on the page.

paper-muted.note: The sidebar ground and the skeleton-row fill. The one place a tonal shift, rather than a hairline, marks a region.

muted-ink.note: Labels, table headers, descriptions, inactive nav items. Roughly 70% of all text on screen.

subtle-ink.note: The quietest legible tier: the em dash standing for an absent value, nav group captions, field notes, trace IDs. 4.85:1 on Paper, 5.76:1 on dark surface. Raised from 0.63/0.57, which were 3.50:1 and 4.18:1 at an 11px size with no large-text exemption.

rule.note: The hairline. Applied globally to `*` as the default border colour, so any element that grows a border grows the right one.

rule-strong.note: A rule doing extra work: a selected stat card, a hovered interactive card, the ring around an unrecognised status literal.

hover.note: The interaction ground for a pointer. Deliberately one step lighter than Selected so a hovered row and a selected row are never confusable.

selected.note: Persistent selection: the active nav item, the row currently previewed in the drawer, a chosen stat filter.

status-neutral-bg.note: Bucket 1 of 6. Closed without incident, or no state worth reporting. WAIVED lives here.

status-neutral-fg.note: Foreground of the neutral bucket. Pairs only with Slate Ground.

status-pending-bg.note: Bucket 2 of 6. Waiting on someone. REOPENED lives here.

status-active-bg.note: Bucket 3 of 6. Live and running normally: in force, in progress.

status-success-bg.note: Bucket 4 of 6. A good terminal outcome. LOADED lives here: an acceptance, with premium loading.

status-warning-bg.note: Bucket 5 of 6. Unresolved, needs a person. IN_DOUBT, POSTPONED and IN_GRACE all live here.

status-danger-bg.note: Bucket 6 of 6. Failed, refused or forced. FORCED_LAPSE_TRIGGERED lives here. Also the ground of the danger button.

status-danger-fg.note: Foreground of the danger bucket, and the ground of the danger button variant.

display.purpose: The stat-card figure, and nothing else. Exactly one occurrence in the codebase, by design.

headline.purpose: The page <h1> in PageHeader. One occurrence, because one component owns it.

title.purpose: Slide-over title and the heaviest in-panel headings.

body.purpose: The content tier: table cell values, form control text, buttons, nav items, gate titles. Reserved for what carries the answer. 98 uses.

label.purpose: The most-used size in the system by a wide margin (226 uses) and the true default for chrome: table headers, field labels, descriptions, stat labels. The compression is a confirmed density decision, not drift.

micro.purpose: Notes, error messages, badge counts, trace IDs, stat hints. The legibility floor.

eyebrow.purpose: Sidebar group captions and gate-panel titles. The only uppercase in the system, and it is structural labelling, never a marketing device.

mono.purpose: Trace IDs and machine identifiers. Selectable, not decorative.

shadows.name: floating-layer
shadows.purpose: The right-hand slide-over only. Paired with a left hairline and a black/20 backdrop (black/50 in dark), because the shadow alone does not separate reliably against a dark ground.

shadows.name: floating-menu
shadows.purpose: Popovers: the date picker and the party picker. Nothing else in the system carries a shadow.

motion.name: colors
motion.purpose: The default and near-only transition. Applied to buttons, nav items, table rows and stat cards. No transform, no lift.

motion.name: overlay
motion.purpose: Slide-over slide-in-from-right plus backdrop fade. The single longest motion in the product.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: The loading spinner. Shown only when a value is genuinely in flight.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: Skeleton rows at staggered widths, so a table does not jump when real data lands.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.note: The only breakpoint doing real work: reveals table columns marked `secondary`. Below it, the identifying column always survives.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.note: Stat row steps from two columns to four.

focus.purpose: Applied globally via :focus-visible. Visible for keyboard users, never suppressed on any control.

narrative.overview:
This console is a bound accounting ledger rendered in software. Ink on paper, ruled hairlines, figures standing in true columns, and colour used only where a clerk would once have reached for a coloured stamp. Nothing here is decorative, because nothing in a ledger ever was: the beauty is in the ruling, the alignment and the fact that the totals can be trusted. A staff member spends their whole working day inside this surface, so it is built to be read rather than admired, and to be read for eight hours without fatigue.

The doctrine that gives the world its edge is inherited straight from the product: render only what the platform can prove. There are no analytics endpoints on this platform, so there are no trend arrows, no sparklines and no percentage deltas. The stat row shows counts. A status the build has never seen is ringed and flagged rather than quietly dressed as a neutral. An absent value is an em dash, never a grey pill reading "Unknown". This refusal is not a limitation the design works around — it is the design's argument, and it is what makes the console feel like a record instead of a dashboard.

Character is confident and tactile. The palette is achromatic and the structure is flat, but the controls should feel pressable and the boundaries should feel drawn on purpose — a ledger is a physical object, and the pen has weight. This is a deliberate small step forward from the incumbent build, which is quieter than this: hover today is a background-colour swap and little else. Where this file states a tactile behaviour that the code has not yet grown, it is stating the target, and the gap is a backlog item rather than licence to invent a different world. The system is emphatically not soft, rounded, playful, gradient-lit or glassy, and it carries no insurer's brand — several insurers are tenants of the same console, so the identity belongs to the platform.
keyCharacteristics: Achromatic by default; six status hues are the entire chromatic vocabulary
Hairline rules and tonal surfaces carry all structure — no shadows at rest
Tabular figures globally, so every money and date column reads as a column
A compressed, functional type scale that prizes density over display
Dark mode is a first-class peer, not a filter: every token is defined twice

rules.name: The Six Buckets Rule
rules.body: Six status buckets are the complete chromatic vocabulary of this system. A seventh bucket is never added; a new backend enum is mapped onto an existing one, and if it genuinely fits none, that is a product conversation and not a colour decision.

rules.name: The Stamp Rule
rules.body: Colour reports state and does nothing else. It never marks hierarchy, never brands a section, never highlights a call to action, and never decorates. A screen on which nothing notable is happening is entirely achromatic — and that emptiness is information.

rules.name: The Both Themes Rule
rules.body: Every colour is declared as a token in :root and redefined in .dark. A component never branches on theme and never hard-codes a hex. A colour that exists in only one theme is not finished.

rules.name: The Inverted-Pair Rule
rules.body: When a status hue is used as a solid ground, its foreground is the matching -bg token, never white. The pair inverts together across themes, so text-white on a -fg ground would be white-on-light in dark mode.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set on body and is never overridden. Every figure in this product is meant to be compared vertically against the figure above it.

rules.name: The Two-Peaks Rule
rules.body: Exactly two type sizes above body exist on any screen: the page headline and, on list screens, the stat figure. A screen that grows a third display size has invented a hierarchy the system does not have.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Is-Structure Rule
rules.body: Uppercase marks a navigational or sectional group caption. It is never used for a button, a badge, a status, or emphasis.

rules.name: The 24 Rule
rules.body: The page gutter is 24px, and every element that meets the page edge aligns to it — header, stat row, empty state, error panel. An element that sets its own page margin has broken the ledger's ruling.

rules.name: The 44px Row Rule
rules.body: A table row is 44px and the activation control fills it. Row height and touch target are one number, so they cannot drift apart.

rules.name: The Floating-Layer Rule
rules.body: A shadow means 'this element is not on the page.' If the element is on the page, it has a hairline and no shadow. There is no third option, and there is no such thing as a subtle resting elevation here.

rules.name: The Pill-for-State Rule
rules.body: Full radius is reserved for elements reporting a state. A fully-rounded button would be lying about what it is.

rules.name: The One-Radius Rule
rules.body: 6px unless there is a stated reason. Two radii inside one component is a mistake, not a texture.

dos: Do define every new colour twice — in :root and in .dark. A token that exists in one theme is unfinished.
Do map a new backend enum onto one of the six existing status buckets, and take the literal from the OpenAPI spec or the Java enum rather than typing it from memory.
Do right-align every numeric column and leave the global tabular-nums alone.
Do align anything meeting the page edge to the 24px gutter.
Do put a wide table in its own overflow-x container so the page body never scrolls sideways.
Do make an activatable row a real <button> in the first cell, filling the 44px row height.
Do render an absent value as an em dash in Subtle Ink, and label it for screen readers when the absence is meaningful.
Do give an icon-only control an aria-label, and give any badge or marker that carries meaning by colour a screen-reader text equivalent.
Do use the outline button as the default and reserve Ledger Ink for the one action the screen exists to perform.
donts: Don't hard-code a hex, an oklch() or an rgb() in a component. Every colour is a token; the sole sanctioned exception is the hashed avatar hue, which is computed from an identifier.
Don't add a seventh status bucket, or use a status hue for anything that is not a status.
Don't add a trend arrow, sparkline, percentage delta or any aggregate this platform has no endpoint for. Counts only.
Don't put a mutating action inside the slide-over. If it changes money, cover or a case, it belongs on a page.
Don't give anything a resting shadow. Shadow means 'floating above the page', and the only floating things are the slide-over and popovers.
Don't introduce a third display size on a screen. Two peaks: the page headline, and the stat figure.
Don't use uppercase for anything but a group caption.
Don't suppress the :focus-visible outline, on any control, ever.
Don't introduce a tenant name, tenant switcher or per-insurer branding. Tenancy is invisible by design and the console is white-label by requirement.
Don't render a grey 'Unknown' pill for a missing status, or a spinner for a value whose load has already failed.
Don't copy the input class string into a new file. It is already duplicated past seventy times; the next one should be extracting the component, not adding to the count.
